paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan ben Yose ben Lakunya — [Shevuot 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.18b.4). Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yose ben Lakunya — [Shabbat 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.49b.7). See his entry.[^4]

notes.text: The abbreviation כ״ל after the first name remains unresolved.

The saved whole Davidson Shevuot18b paragraph explicitly names Rabbi Yonatan ben Yose ben Lakunya asking Rabbi Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya. It supports a contextual ben Lakunya comparison for כ״ל, not a proved כ/ב letter history. The old see gloss is superseded additively. The father’s title remains abbreviated R'; the separate Shabbat49b occurrence has not been inspected here, so its Shimon/Yose titles remain R' without borrowing an expanded title from another citation.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 733) reads ב״ל where the supplied Hebrew has כ״ל. In Shevuot 18b, Rabbi Yonatan ben Yose ben Lakunya asks Rabbi Shimon ben Yose ben Lakunya. In Shabbat 49b, Rabbi Yonatan son of Rabbi Elazar reports the teaching of Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yose ben Lakunya. These are distinct reporting contexts.

Heilprin’s [Yonatan entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1882&lang=en) treats Yonatan as Shimon’s brother in the Shevuot exchange. His [Shimon entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3452&lang=en) also discusses the distinct Shabbat report, in which Rabbi Yonatan son of Rabbi Elazar quotes Shimon. The two passages name their speakers differently.
